thread:
rachel: heads-up: noticed a short cluster of "duplicate" streams this morning on several EU shards. console spiked active_streams for single client IDs. snippet from runtime log: ```INFO sse.runtime: accept tenant=glint client_id=svc:77 resume_token=present prev_shard=shard-3 allocated_shard=shard-9 new_session=sess-9abc outcome=allocated_new```
anjay: was this correlated with the deploy at 07:00? billing?
rachel: not a deploy. billing pipeline shows no double charges. this looks like resume tokens being presented but failing to attach because routing landed them on a shard that doesn't have the lease. runtime then creates a fresh session. console treats the new session as an independent connection and alerts.
frank: so two problems: operator confusion/alerts and lack of explicit telemetry that a resume was attempted. agree we should emit a low-cardinality outcome metric.
anjay: propose: metrics.counter('sse.session_start', tags={ 'outcome': 'resume|accepted|fallback', 'region': 'eu' }) — keep tenant out of this metric to avoid cardinality explosion. detailed logs can still include tenant for SRE.
rachel: add a sampled diagnostic log when token present but new session created. include prev_shard, new_shard, client_ip_hash and a tiny reason code. sample at 0.5%. example: ```diag.emit('sse.resume_mismatch', {prev_shard:'shard-3', new_shard:'shard-9', ip_hash:'h_xxx', reason:'lease-miss'})```
frank: console UX: show a subtle gray "resumed"/"new" label in the connections table. Label = "resumed" if token presented AND previous session last_seen < 20s AND token valid. Hover text: "Client reattached using resume token; routing fallback allocated a new backend session. Billing unaffected." Put behind FF.
anjay: watch out for NAT: many clients behind same IP will look like resumes. the label must be opt-in behind FF and we should measure false_positive_rate (FP = label && distinct ip_hash).
sre-bot: alert sse.duplicate_connections suppressed at 2026-03-27T09:12:03Z for route eu-iso (auto-resolved)
frank: rollout plan: 1) telemetry metric + sampled diag (telemetry-only canary 5% tenants), 2) alert rule tweak to ignore dup spikes correlated with high resume_ratio, 3) console FF + internal canary, 4) expand. Monitor resume_ratio, FP rate, and alert fidelity.
rachel: short-term alert change: modify alert to add exception when resume_ratio > 0.4 within the 1m window. frank: I'll prep PR for alert rule.
anjay: implementation notes: don't add outcome tag to high-cardinality per-tenant metrics. Use outcome only on derived counters. For tracing, keep payload tiny and never include full headers.
frank: runbook update: when you see duplicate streams, check resume_ratio and ip_hash distributions, then verify recent shard routing changes. If resume_ratio low and duplicates persist, escalate to runtime.
pm: quick UX ask: can you make the tooltip explicit that billing unaffected? product prefers "This does not indicate double billing."
rachel: will include that exact copy in console PR. console-bot: created ticket PLAT-9577 "SSE resume/fallback telemetry + UI label" assigned to rachel, anjay, frank
anjay: I'll schedule the telemetry canary for 08:30 UTC tomorrow. keep diag sampling low to avoid hot-path overhead.
frank: action items recap: rachel -> console copy + PR behind FF; anjay -> telemetry PR + diag emitter; frank -> alert rule PR + runbook entry. monitor canary and post results in #release-war-room.
